title: Green Propolis as a Candidate Bio-Based Seed-Treatment Material for Common Bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.): Exposure-Time Responses and One Health Implications
content: Bio-based seed treatments may contribute to more sustainable agricultural inputs, but their efficacy and safety require evaluation. This study assessed green propolis for common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.), examining elemental and physicochemical properties and exposure-duration effects on germination and early seedling development. Propolis elemental composition was analyzed by wavelength-dispersive X-ray fluorescence (WDXRF), while aqueous and hydroalcoholic extracts were characterized by UV–Vis spectrophotometry, pH, qualitative phytochemical screening, and dynamic light scattering. XRF revealed a mineral profile dominated by potassium, calcium, and phosphorus. The selected filtered aqueous extract, heated at 60 °C for 5 min (EPFA3), had near-neutral pH and a mean zeta potential of −39.8 mV. Seeds were exposed to EPFA3 for 10, 30, or 120 min and compared with untreated controls. Germination was 89,9% in the control and 72.2%, 55.6%, and 16.7% after 10, 30, and 120 min, respectively. Most seedling growth and biomass parameters did not differ significantly among treatments. These results indicate an exposure-time-dependent response and do not demonstrate a consistent biostimulant effect under the tested conditions.
